**Expected goals (xG) is the probability that an unblocked shot becomes a goal, given where it was taken from, how it was taken, and what happened just before it.** A tip-in from the crease might carry an xG of 0.25; a wrist shot from the point, 0.02. Add xG up over a game or a season and you get the number of goals an average shooter would have scored on those chances. The gap between goals and xG separates finishing and goaltending from shot generation.

This article explains the model behind the `xg` column in `fastRhockey`'s NHL play-by-play: what it predicts, which features it uses, how it was trained, how well it does, and where it is weakest. Every number in a code block below is computed when the page is built. Numbers from training are quoted from the [official model card](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/fastRhockey-nhl-data/blob/main/docs/models/nhl_xg.md) and labelled that way.

The PWHL has its own, different model. See the [PWHL expected goals article](pwhl-expected-goals-xg-model.html).

<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert">

**Changed in fastRhockey 1.1.0.** NHL `x_fixed` / `y_fixed` now rotate the rink by the NHL API's `homeTeamDefendingSide`, so the home team always shoots right. Before 1.1.0 every home-team event got `x_fixed = abs(x)` and every away-team event `-abs(x)`, which mirrored any play from a team's own half into its attacking half. That changes `shot_distance`, `shot_angle` and the previous-event features, and so xG, for NHL play-by-play. The models were retrained on 2026-11-13 on a corpus built with the same rotation. The [coordinates section](#how-are-the-coordinates-set) shows the result in the data.

</div>

## Which xG are you looking at?

There are two ways to get NHL xG from `fastRhockey`. They use the same model files and, as shown [below](#do-the-published-values-match-a-local-run), give the same numbers.

| | Published `xg` column | Computed locally |
|---|---|---|
| **How you get it** | `load_nhl_pbp()`, `load_nhl_pbp_full()` | `nhl_game_pbp()` / `nhl_game_feed()`, or `helper_nhl_calculate_xg()` on your own frame |
| **Model** | The boosters in the `nhl_xg_models` release (retrained 2026-11-13) | The same boosters, downloaded on first use, checked against the sha256s in the release manifest (`xg_model_meta.json`) and cached |
| **Needs `xgboost`?** | No | Yes. Without it `nhl_game_pbp()` and `helper_nhl_calculate_xg()` warn (class `fastRhockey_no_xgboost`) and return `xg = NA`. |
| **When it changes** | When a season file is rescored after a retrain | On the first xG call of a session after a retrain: the cached files no longer match the release manifest, so they are replaced. `refresh_xg_models()` forces a fresh download. |

Two practical notes on `helper_nhl_calculate_xg()`:

- **A frame may hold several games.** Predictions are joined back by `game_id` and `event_id`, so the rows and their order are kept, and an existing `xg` column is replaced.
- The model files live in `tools::R_user_dir("fastRhockey", "cache")`. Each session re-reads the small release manifest; files that still match it are not downloaded again. Offline, the last manifest seen and its cached files are used. `refresh_xg_models()` deletes the files and downloads the current versions.

## What does the model predict?

The model scores **unblocked shot attempts**, the events hockey analysts call Fenwick events: `SHOT` (on goal), `MISSED_SHOT` and `GOAL`. Blocked shots never reach the goalie, so they get no xG. Before scoring, the feature builder (`helper_nhl_prepare_xg_data()`) drops:

- shootout attempts (`period_type == "SHOOTOUT"`);
- penalty shots, which get a constant instead (below);
- line changes (`CHANGE`), so the "previous event" is always a hockey play;
- shots whose previous event is not one of `FACEOFF`, `GIVEAWAY`, `TAKEAWAY`, `BLOCKED_SHOT`, `HIT`, `MISSED_SHOT`, `SHOT`, `STOP`, `PENALTY` or `GOAL`.

The output is three components:

1. **A 5v5 model**, for every shot where `strength_state == "5v5"`.
2. **A special-teams model**, for every other strength state: power play, shorthanded, 4v4, 3v3 and empty-net situations such as 6v5.
3. **A penalty-shot constant**, the historical conversion rate of penalty shots, assigned to every penalty shot.

Both models are XGBoost binary classifiers with a log-loss objective. They follow the recipe of Daniel Morse's [hockeyR](https://github.com/danmorse314/hockeyR) xG model, re-fit on the `fastRhockey` NHL corpus.

## Which features does it use?

All features are built in `helper_nhl_prepare_xg_data()` from the play-by-play columns listed in `?nhl_xg`.

| Group | Features | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Shot geometry | `shot_distance`, `shot_angle` | Feet and degrees to the attacked net (at x = ±89 ft) |
| Shot type | `wrist_shot`, `snap_shot`, `slap_shot`, `backhand`, `tip_in`, `deflected`, `wrap_around`, `poke`, `batted`, `between_legs`, `cradle` | One-hot. The newer NHL API's lowercase types (`wrist`, `tip-in`, `bat`, ...) are mapped back to the older title-case names the model was trained on |
| Previous event | `last_faceoff`, `last_shot`, `last_missed_shot`, `last_blocked_shot`, `last_giveaway`, `last_takeaway`, `last_hit`, `last_stop`, `last_penalty`, `last_goal` | One-hot type of the event before the shot, within the same game and period |
| Pre-shot movement | `time_since_last`, `distance_from_last`, `last_x`, `last_y` | Seconds and feet since the previous event, and where it happened |
| Tactical flags | `rebound`, `rush`, `cross_ice_event` | Rebound: previous event an unblocked shot within 2 s. Rush: previous event in the neutral or defensive zone within 4 s. Cross-ice: previous event in the offensive zone on the other side of the ice (`y` crossing ±3 ft) within 2 s |
| Game state | `empty_net` | The shot was at an empty net |
| Era | `era_2011_2013`, `era_2014_2018`, `era_2019_2021`, `era_2022_2024`, `era_2025_on` | One-hot season buckets, so rule and tracking changes are modelled instead of averaged away |
| Special teams only | `total_skaters_on`, `event_team_advantage` | Skaters on the ice, and the shooting team's skater edge |

You can read the exact feature lists out of the cached model metadata.

```{r load_pkg}
library(fastRhockey)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

xg_env <- fastRhockey:::.xg_env
# The models load on first use; load them here (a download the first time).
xg_ready <- requireNamespace("xgboost", quietly = TRUE) &&
  !inherits(try(fastRhockey:::.load_xg_models(), silent = TRUE), "try-error") &&
  !is.null(xg_env$xg_model_5v5)
xg_ready
```

```{r feature_lists, eval = xg_ready}
xg_env$xg_feature_names_5v5

setdiff(xg_env$xg_feature_names_st, xg_env$xg_feature_names_5v5)

# the penalty-shot constant
xg_env$xg_model_ps
```

### What does the 5v5 model lean on?

Gain is the share of the model's total loss reduction that comes from splits on each feature.

```{r importance, eval = xg_ready}
imp <- xgboost::xgb.importance(model = xg_env$xg_model_5v5)
head(imp[, c("Feature", "Gain")], 12)
```

```{r importance_plot, eval = xg_ready, fig.alt = "Horizontal bar chart of the twelve features with the highest gain in the NHL 5v5 expected goals model."}
imp %>%
  head(12) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Gain, y = reorder(Feature, Gain))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#531896") +
  labs(
    title = "NHL 5v5 xG model: feature importance (gain)",
    x = "Share of total gain", y = NULL,
    caption = "Data: fastRhockey xG model files"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Distance dominates, as in every public xG model. Empty net ranks high because it is rare but decisive. Shot type and the time since the previous event come next.

## How was it trained?

As reported in the [model card](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/fastRhockey-nhl-data/blob/main/docs/models/nhl_xg.md) and its model registry:

- **Data:** the NHL play-by-play corpus of the [fastRhockey-nhl-data](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/fastRhockey-nhl-data) repository, 18 seasons from 2009-10 to 2026-27 (2026-27 in progress at training time), grouped into the five era buckets above (2009-10 is the reference era). The corpus was rebuilt with the 1.1.0 rink rotation before the fit. The 5v5 model is fit on 5v5 shots only; the special-teams model on every other strength state.
- **Split:** an 80/20 train/holdout split grouped by `game_id` (no game appears on both sides), seed 37, with grouped 5-fold cross-validation on the training side.
- **Algorithm:** XGBoost, binary log-loss.
- **Fit in use:** retrained on 2026-11-13 (release manifest `version` 2026-11-13).
- **Cross-validation:** 5v5 CV AUC **0.782** and CV log-loss **0.1906**; special teams CV AUC **0.7574** and CV log-loss **0.2806**.
- **Held-out games:** on the 20% of games kept out of training, AUC **0.7819** (5v5, log-loss 0.1908 against a 0.2213 constant baseline) and **0.7607** (special teams, log-loss 0.2772 against 0.3272). Per season on those games, goals divided by summed xG stays between about 0.93 and 1.03 at 5v5.

## How well does it do on 2025-26?

Below, the published `xg` column is scored against the 2025-26 regular season. That season is in the training corpus (about 80% of its games were in the training split), so read this as a sanity check, not a holdout.

```{r load_pbp}
pbp <- load_nhl_pbp(seasons = 2026)

shots <- pbp %>%
  filter(season_type == "R", !is.na(xg)) %>%
  mutate(
    goal = as.integer(event_type == "GOAL"),
    model = if_else(strength_state == "5v5", "5v5", "special teams")
  )

rank_auc <- function(y, p) {
  r <- rank(p)
  n1 <- sum(y == 1)
  n0 <- sum(y == 0)
  (sum(r[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}
log_loss <- function(y, p) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)
  -mean(y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p))
}

eval_tbl <- shots %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    shots = n(),
    goals = sum(goal),
    sum_xg = round(sum(xg), 1),
    goals_per_xg = round(goals / sum(xg), 3),
    log_loss = round(log_loss(goal, xg), 4),
    baseline_log_loss = round(log_loss(goal, rep(mean(goal), n())), 4),
    rank_auc = round(rank_auc(goal, xg), 4),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
eval_tbl
```

On this season the 5v5 model ranks shots with an AUC of `r eval_tbl$rank_auc[eval_tbl$model == "5v5"]` and beats a constant-rate baseline on log-loss. Goals divided by xG is `r eval_tbl$goals_per_xg[eval_tbl$model == "5v5"]` at 5v5 and `r eval_tbl$goals_per_xg[eval_tbl$model == "special teams"]` on special teams; a value of 1 means summed xG matches actual goals.

### Is it calibrated?

A calibrated model's shots with xG near 0.10 go in about 10% of the time. Here the shots are split into ten equal-sized bins by xG.

```{r calibration, fig.alt = "Calibration plot of NHL expected goals by decile for 2025-26, actual goal rate against mean xG, with a dashed diagonal."}
calib <- shots %>%
  group_by(model, decile = ntile(xg, 10)) %>%
  summarise(mean_xg = mean(xg), goal_rate = mean(goal), shots = n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(calib, aes(x = mean_xg, y = goal_rate, colour = model)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("5v5" = "#531896", "special teams" = "#368EAF")) +
  labs(
    title = "Calibration by xG decile, 2025-26 regular season",
    x = "Mean xG in decile", y = "Actual goal rate", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Data: fastRhockey::load_nhl_pbp()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### How does xG fall off with distance?

```{r distance_curve, fig.alt = "Line chart of mean expected goals and actual goal rate by shot distance bin for 2025-26 5v5 NHL shots."}
shots %>%
  filter(model == "5v5", !empty_net, shot_distance <= 90) %>%
  mutate(distance_bin = cut(shot_distance, breaks = seq(0, 90, 5))) %>%
  group_by(distance_bin) %>%
  summarise(`Mean xG` = mean(xg), `Goal rate` = mean(goal), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-distance_bin) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = distance_bin, y = value, colour = name, group = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Mean xG" = "#531896", "Goal rate" = "#37C4E3")) +
  labs(
    title = "5v5 xG and goal rate by shot distance, 2025-26",
    subtitle = "Non-empty-net unblocked shots",
    x = "Shot distance (ft)", y = NULL, colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Do the published values match a local run?

Yes. This recomputes xG for the first 30 regular-season games with `helper_nhl_calculate_xg()`, one game at a time, and compares it with the published column.

```{r reproduce, eval = xg_ready}
games <- sort(unique(pbp$game_id[pbp$season_type == "R"]))[1:30]

local_xg <- pbp %>%
  filter(game_id %in% games) %>%
  rename(xg_published = xg) %>%
  group_split(game_id) %>%
  lapply(function(g) helper_nhl_calculate_xg(as.data.frame(g))) %>%
  bind_rows()

local_xg %>%
  filter(!is.na(xg) | !is.na(xg_published)) %>%
  summarise(
    shots = n(),
    both_present = sum(!is.na(xg) & !is.na(xg_published)),
    max_abs_diff = max(abs(xg - xg_published), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

A `max_abs_diff` of 0 means the published `xg` is exactly what the package computes with the current model files. A larger value means the season file was scored with a different set of models from the one in your cache.

## How are the coordinates set?

`x_fixed` puts the home team shooting right. Shots should then sit almost entirely at the attacked end (`x_fixed > 0` for the home team, `< 0` for the away team), while hits and giveaways, which happen all over the ice, split roughly evenly. A blocked shot's event team is the blocker, so it sits at the blocker's own end.

```{r coord_issue}
pbp %>%
  filter(
    event_type %in% c("HIT", "BLOCKED_SHOT", "GIVEAWAY", "SHOT"),
    !is.na(x_fixed), x != 0
  ) %>%
  group_by(event_type, event_team_type) %>%
  summarise(
    events = n(),
    share_raw_x_positive = round(mean(x > 0), 3),
    share_x_fixed_positive = round(mean(x_fixed > 0), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Plays for which the feed gives no side use the period's side, then where each team's shots cluster. `shot_distance` and `shot_angle` for a `BLOCKED_SHOT` are measured to the shooter's target net.

## Where are the estimates weakest?

- **Season-level drift.** The era indicators absorb most rule and tracking changes, and per-season calibration on held-out games stays within about 7% at 5v5, but a new season can drift before the next retrain (an annual July run in fastRhockey-nhl-data). Check `goals / sum(xg)` before treating xG totals as goal-scale.
- **No pre-shot passing data.** Public NHL feeds do not record passes or screens, so one-timers and royal-road passes are under-rated by construction.
- **Rink and scorer effects.** Shot locations are recorded by arena scorers. No rink adjustment is applied.
- **Small special-teams samples.** The special-teams model has a little over a quarter of the 5v5 training shots, so treat it as noisier.

## How do I reproduce this?

```{r reproduce_steps, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("fastRhockey", "xgboost"))
library(fastRhockey)

# published xG, a whole season
pbp <- load_nhl_pbp(seasons = 2026)

# live play-by-play for one game, with xG computed locally
game <- nhl_game_pbp(game_id = 2025020001)

# your own frame (one or many games)
pbp_xg <- helper_nhl_calculate_xg(pbp)

# force a fresh download of the cached model files
refresh_xg_models()
```

The training code, evaluation notebook and model files are in [fastRhockey-nhl-data](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/fastRhockey-nhl-data). The model card is [docs/models/nhl_xg.md](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/fastRhockey-nhl-data/blob/main/docs/models/nhl_xg.md).
